# Is a Treadmill Good for Weight Loss? What 30 Minutes a Day Really Does (Backed by Science)


Last updated November 2026


Turning up the incline is the quickest way to make 30 minutes on a treadmill burn more.


**Short answer:** Yes. A treadmill is one of the best-studied tools for weight loss. In a 10-month trial where adults exercised mostly on treadmills five days a week without dieting, they lost 8.6 to 11.5 pounds while a non-exercising group gained weight. Thirty minutes a day helps, especially with some incline, and it works best alongside modest changes to what you eat, kept up for months.


The details matter, because the number on the calorie counter, the 30 minutes you have and the weight you actually lose rarely line up as neatly as you'd hope. And most treadmill weight-loss attempts stall long before the science gets a chance to work, for reasons the studies explain pretty well.

## Is a Treadmill Good for Weight Loss?


Yes, and the evidence is unusually solid. Treadmills are what researchers use when they want to control exactly how much exercise people do, so the biggest weight-loss trials read like a log of treadmill workouts.


Study What people did What happened


[Midwest Exercise Trial 2](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23592678/) (2013), 141 adults, 10 months Supervised exercise five days a week, mostly walking or jogging on treadmills, burning 400 or 600 calories a session. No diet changes. Lost 3.9 kg (8.6 lb) and 5.2 kg (11.5 lb). The non-exercising group gained 0.5 kg.


[Jakicic et al., JAMA](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10546695/) (1999), 148 women, 18 months A weight-loss program with diet changes, plus short bouts of exercise. One group also got a treadmill at home. The home-treadmill group lost 7.4 kg (16 lb), twice as much as the same plan without one (3.7 kg), and kept exercising more in months 13 to 18.


[E-MECHANIC](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31172175/) (2019), 198 adults, 24 weeks Supervised exercise at a low or high weekly dose Both groups lost less than their workouts predicted, mostly because they started eating 90 to 124 more calories a day.


[Wewege et al.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28401638/) (2017), 13 trials Interval training vs steady cardio in adults with overweight or obesity Both cut body fat. Running-based training had large effects, and intervals took about 40% less time.


[Vissers et al.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23409182/) (2013), 15 studies Exercise programs without dieting Aerobic exercise reduced visceral (deep belly) fat, with changes visible after 12 weeks.


Exercise alone works, just slowly: the MET-2 volunteers kept eating as usual and still lost about 4 to 6% of their body weight in 10 months. The people who kept going longest also lost the most. In the JAMA trial, women who logged more than 200 minutes a week lost an average of 13.1 kg (about 29 pounds) over 18 months, against 3.5 kg (about 8 pounds) for those under 150 minutes.


## How Many Calories Does 30 Minutes on a Treadmill Burn?


It depends on three things: your body weight, your speed and, more than most people expect, the incline. Here are estimates for 30 minutes, worked out with the American College of Sports Medicine's standard walking and running equations and rounded to the nearest 5:


30-minute workout 150 lb 180 lb 210 lb


Easy walk: 3.0 mph, flat 120 140 165


Brisk walk: 3.5 mph, flat 130 160 185


Incline walk: 3.0 mph, 5% 190 230 270


Incline walk: 3.0 mph, 10% 265 320 370


12-3-30: 3.0 mph, 12% 295 355 415


Jog: 5.0 mph, flat 310 370 435


Run: 6.0 mph, flat 365 435 510


At the same easy 3 mph, a 10% grade more than doubles the burn of a flat walk, and the[12-3-30 workout](https://www.avironactive.com/blog/12-3-30-treadmill-workout/) lands close to a 5 mph jog without a single running stride. That makes incline the best deal on a treadmill for anyone who doesn't love running.


Three caveats before you trust any calorie number, ours included:


- These are totals. For a 180-pound person, about 40 of those calories are what you'd burn sitting on the couch for half an hour anyway.
- Gripping the handrails cuts the burn. In a[University of Wisconsin study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17135860/) , it lowered oxygen use, a direct proxy for calories, by roughly 15 to 21% at the same speed and grade.
- Your treadmill's calorie count comes from a formula like this one, so it's only as good as the body weight you've entered.


## What Does 30 Minutes a Day on a Treadmill Really Do?


Thirty minutes every day adds up to 210 minutes a week. The American College of Sports Medicine's[position stand on weight loss](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19127177/) says 150 to 250 minutes a week of moderate activity prevents weight gain and gives "only modest weight loss." Clinically significant loss from exercise has been linked to more than 250 minutes a week.


In other words, 30 minutes of comfortable flat walking will do more for your health than for the scale. Two changes make the same half hour count for weight loss.


**1. Make the 30 minutes harder.** The lower-dose group in MET-2 burned 400 calories a session. For a 180-pound person, that's about 35 minutes at 3 mph on a 12% incline. On the flat at a brisk 3.5 mph, it takes well over an hour.


**2. Watch what happens after the workout.** In E-MECHANIC, the people who exercised most ate about 124 extra calories a day, enough to wipe out 2.7 kg (about 6 pounds) of the loss their workouts should have produced over 24 weeks. Their metabolism didn't slow and they didn't move less during the rest of the day; they simply got hungrier. Decide on your post-workout snack before you step on the belt.


Then give it time. NIH researchers have[shown](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21872751/) that body weight responds slowly to a change in calories, taking about a year to get halfway to its new level. The NIH's[Body Weight Planner](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/bwp) lets you enter your own numbers, including new exercise, and see a realistic timeline.

## Walking, Incline or Running: Which Treadmill Workout Burns the Most Fat?


Per minute, running burns the most, incline walking comes a close second and flat walking comes last. Over a few months the ranking can flip, because the best weight-loss workout is the one you're still doing in March.


### Incline Walking: The Most Burn for the Least Pounding


Incline adds work without adding speed or impact. A[2025 University of Nevada, Las Vegas study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39917588/) compared the 12-3-30 with self-paced running at the same total calories. The 12-3-30 took longer to get there, but more of its energy came from fat. Total calories still decide weight loss, so there's no magic fat-burning zone here, but a steep walk is a strong option if you're just starting out or your knees don't love running.

### Running and Intervals: The Fastest Burn


Running wins on time. In the[National Runners' and Walkers' Health Study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23190592/) , which followed more than 47,000 people for about six years, running was linked to more weight loss than walking for the same energy spent, up to 90% more among the heaviest participants. And in the 2017 meta-analysis above, intervals matched steady cardio for fat loss in about 40% less time. ### Flat Walking: The One People Stick With


Flat walking burns the least per minute, but it's easy to start and hard to quit. In that same six-year study, walkers' activity dropped far less over time than runners' did. If running would make you skip workouts, walk. Then add incline.


## How Often Should You Use a Treadmill to Lose Weight?


Aim for five or six days a week, starting around 150 minutes and building past 250. Mix the three workout types so no two days in a row feel the same. Here's a sample week, with programs from the Aviron app you can follow on any of our treadmills:

Tue Incline walk 30 min, 3 mph, 8 to 12% Calorie Crush or Ascent


Wed Intervals 20 to 25 min, fast and easy blocks HIIT Walks or HIIT Running


Thu Easy walk 20 to 30 min, conversational pace Beach Sunset or Paderne


Fri Climb 20 to 30 min, building to 12% Walkathon with coach Jenny Ferrero, or SkyQuest


Sat Long walk or race 45 min or more Long Walks, or race-walk an Olympic medalist like Daniel Pintado

That's roughly 180 minutes. Add 5 minutes to each session every week or two until you're past 250. If you have a medical condition or haven't exercised in a while, check with your doctor before you ramp up.


No 30-minute block in your day? Split it. In the JAMA trial, the women doing short bouts did best when they had a treadmill at home, losing twice as much as the short-bout group without one. A 10-minute[walk after dinner](https://www.avironactive.com/blog/walking-after-eating/) counts. So does a slow walk through your inbox.

## Why Do Most People Stop Losing Weight on a Treadmill?


Usually because they stop using the treadmill. Every study above shows it works for people who keep at it. The first week is great, the third week is a chore, and by month two the treadmill is an expensive clothes rack.


We call that the motivation cliff, and it isn't a willpower problem. Your phone was engineered to be hard to put down. Most treadmills were engineered to be a belt and a speed button. The research points the same way: the women with a treadmill at home kept exercising longer, and the people who logged the most minutes lost the most weight.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is 30 minutes on a treadmill enough to lose weight?


It's enough to start. Thirty minutes a day is 210 minutes a week, which the American College of Sports Medicine places in the modest weight-loss range on its own. Make some of those sessions incline or intervals, pair them with small diet changes and work up past 250 minutes a week for bigger results.


### Can you lose belly fat on a treadmill?


You can't spot-reduce, but treadmill cardio is good at shrinking the deep belly fat around your organs. A 2013 meta-analysis of 15 studies found aerobic exercise reduced this visceral fat even without dieting, with measurable changes after 12 weeks.


### Is walking or running on a treadmill better for weight loss?


Running burns more per minute, and in a six-year study of more than 47,000 people it was linked to more weight loss for the same energy spent. Walking is easier to keep up. If you can run without dreading it, run some days. If not, walk on an incline.


### Does holding onto the treadmill burn fewer calories?


Yes. Gripping the handrails lowered oxygen use by roughly 15 to 21% in one study, which means fewer calories at the same settings. If you're leaning on the rails to keep up, lower the speed or incline instead. A light hold for balance on a steep climb is a different story.


### How much weight can you lose in a month on a treadmill?


Without changing your diet, expect around a pound a month at first. That's roughly the pace of the 10-month MET-2 trial, where volunteers lost 8.6 to 11.5 pounds. Add diet changes and more minutes and it goes faster. Judge your progress over three months, not three weeks.


### Is walking on a treadmill as good as walking outside?


Close enough. Outdoors you also push through air, which matters more at running speeds, and a[1996 study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8887211/) found a 1% incline makes treadmill running cost the same energy as running outside on flat ground. At walking speeds the gap is small. The bigger advantage is that rain, dark evenings and icy sidewalks can't cancel a treadmill walk.
